He should be found guilty of recklessly causing serious bodily injury (for example, reckless or aggravated battery), not an intentional offense, because his admitted indifference to the consequences of reckless driving satisfies the recklessness mental state even without intent to injure. The facts don't establish intent or the extreme-indifference malice needed for a homicide-level charge, and the exact label depends on the jurisdiction's statutes. The team note about attempted manslaughter is wrong: attempt requires intent to commit the target crime, so it can't be built on recklessness.
